note: Sunday 07:00 SGT weekend sweep, pre-Asia-open and ahead of the Sun-evening 27 Jul oil/futures reopen, after the Fri 24 Jul US close — price levels are as of that close unless noted (oil/metals futures were shut over the weekend; crypto levels are the latest verifiable, ~Fri-Sat). The dominant cross-portfolio driver stays the US-Iran war (13th straight night of US strikes) and the oil-led shift toward pricing a possible 2026 Fed HIKE. Two Sunday-relevant developments moved the read this run: (1) China's 24 Jul Politburo delivered STRONGER-than-expected countercyclical-stimulus language plus an anti-'involution' pricing-law draft — a positive for the HK-tech core, resolving the prior 'await-Politburo' binary to the upside; (2) silver, having broken below $58 Thursday, clawed back to ~$58 by Friday's close. Fresh items (8 of 13) are dated Thu 23–Sat 25 Jul. Every item source-verified against the cited pages; the MAS S-REIT leverage item is flagged as reported-but-pending primary confirmation.

items.headline: China's 24 Jul Politburo signals stronger-than-expected H2 stimulus; anti-'involution' pricing-law draft
items.summary: The 24-member Politburo, chaired by Xi, met on H2 economic work and issued stronger-than-expected wording — pledging countercyclical policy 'with precision and force.' The same day the NDRC and market regulator released a draft amendment to China's pricing law (its first update since 1998) targeting 'disorderly low-price competition' (anti-involution). The signalling lands after Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3%, the weakest in three-plus years.
items.actionable: The binary the book was waiting on resolved to the upside — the Politburo's forceful language and the anti-involution pricing reform support the HK-tech core (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) into earnings. Hold; favor Tencent on relative strength and AI/buyback support, and watch for follow-through detail at the late-Jul/Aug policy meetings before adding.

items.headline: US-Iran war: 13th straight night of US strikes; talks continue but ceasefire in tatters
items.summary: US Central Command carried out a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military and maritime infrastructure. Trump said the two sides remain in talks and Tehran is 'getting more serious' but also warned of an 'unprecedented military response'; Iran denies rejecting an Iraqi-brokered ceasefire and blames Washington. UN chief Guterres has warned the situation is 'getting out of control.'
items.actionable: The single event driving every cross-current: bullish gold/oil and Seatrium's offshore-order backdrop, but the inflation impulse keeps the Fed/MAS hawkish — a headwind for levered silver, S-REITs and HK tech. Watch the binary into the 27 Jul futures reopen: further escalation (Hormuz/Bab-al-Mandab) spikes oil and gold, a genuine de-escalation unwinds the whole rate-sensitive trade.

items.headline: Silver broke below $58 on rate-hike repricing, then clawed back to ~$58; gold ~$4,055
items.summary: Silver fell toward $57 (down >3% intraday the prior session) as surging oil strengthened the case for tighter Fed policy and lifted real yields (10Y ~4.69% close, 4.71% intraday high) and the dollar (DXY ~101.5), before recovering to roughly $58.0-58.4/oz by Friday's close. Gold held below $4,100 at ~$4,055 ahead of the FOMC. For the week, silver still gained ~4.6% on safe-haven and industrial-demand support.
items.actionable: The levered silver core is the portfolio's biggest short-term swing factor — it fell hardest on the rate-hike repricing but reclaimed $58, so the break was not decisive. Silver moves 2-3x gold on shifts in hike expectations, cutting both ways around the 28-29 Jul FOMC; treat the $57-58 zone as the line and consider hedging the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into the print.

items.headline: Oil holds near multi-month highs; Brent ~$97, up >12% on the week; 27 Jul reopen skewed higher
items.summary: Brent slipped ~4% Friday to ~$96.8/bbl (WTI ~$90.5) on US-Iran peace-talk reports but stayed up more than 12% on the week and ~30% on the month on Middle East supply fear. Houthi threats forced at least seven Saudi crude tankers to divert from Bab el-Mandeb, and analysts flag prices biased higher into the Sunday 27 Jul futures reopen. This channel is what forced the hawkish Fed repricing pressuring silver.
items.actionable: Watch the diplomatic thread and the 27 Jul reopen — a de-escalation is the fastest catalyst to unwind rate-hike fear and let levered silver, S-REITs and crypto rebound (bearish the energy long but a tailwind for the far-larger rate-sensitive book). Trade the escalation odds, not the individual legs.

items.headline: FOMC 28-29 Jul preview: hawkish hold base case, but ~34-36% now price a 25bp HIKE
items.summary: The Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh since May 2026) is widely expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting on 28-29 Jul, but oil topping ~$100 mid-week has pushed markets to assign ~34-36% odds to a hike to 3.75-4.00%, with September hike odds above 80%. Hawkish Fedspeak (Cook citing 3.7% inflation; Waller, Jefferson) reinforced the tail. June CPI cooled to 3.5% headline / 2.6% core, but energy keeps the Fed cautious. No SEP at this meeting; decision Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET.
items.actionable: The shift from 'one cut' to a live ~1-in-3 hike is the core near-term threat to levered silver and SGX REITs, keeping rates higher-for-longer. The big USD cash pile (earning ~3.5-3.75%) is an asset here — stay patient and let the oil/rate shock resolve before redeploying into rate-sensitive names; a dovish 29 Jul surprise or an Iran de-escalation is the upside catalyst.

items.headline: Houthi blockade forces Saudi crude tankers to U-turn; Saudi Arabia strikes Houthis in Yemen
items.summary: At least seven Saudi crude tankers reversed course toward Suez after the Houthis emailed shipowners warning against calling at Saudi ports; the broader 2026 Hormuz/Red Sea crisis has damaged ~17 merchant ships. Saudi Arabia said it launched strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen after another Saudi vessel was attacked, widening the conflict beyond the direct US-Iran axis and adding a second front to the shipping/energy disruption.
items.actionable: A widening maritime-supply disruption keeps a floor under oil and a bid under safe-haven gold regardless of the US-Iran talks — the escalation leg of the binary. Reinforces gold-heavy GDX and the energy sleeve; the risk to the rate-sensitive book is that a sustained oil premium hardens the Fed's hawkish tilt.

items.headline: Gold holds ~$4,055 below a $4,130 two-week high as safe-haven demand fights rate crosscurrents
items.summary: Gold hit a two-week high near $4,130 on 22 July on Iran-war safe-haven bids and a softer dollar, then eased to ~$4,055 by 24 July as oil-driven inflation fears and higher yields (10Y ~4.69%) capped it. Dip-buying persisted near $4,050 and gold funds drew ~+$2.0bn in the latest weekly flows, though BofA continues to flag a gold 'death cross' and elevated net-longs into the Fed.
items.actionable: Gold is holding up far better than silver in this regime — favor the gold-heavy miners (GDX) over pure silver leverage while the war/inflation tug-of-war persists. The ~$4,130 high is the level to reclaim; a hawkish Fed or Iran de-escalation could fade it toward $4,000.

items.headline: Singapore banks at record highs as earnings open; DBS guides FY2026 profit slightly lower
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB hit fresh record highs in July (DBS above S$70) on wealth-management fee income cushioning lower rates, ahead of DBS's 6 Aug results. SGX reporting season opened 23 Jul after hours — Mapletree Industrial Trust posted a DPU of 3.11 cents (-4.9% y/y), and CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug. DBS has guided FY2026 net profit slightly below 2025 while reaffirming its 15-cent/quarter capital-return dividend.
items.actionable: SGX banks ride record highs into 6 Aug DBS earnings — supportive for the blue-chip sleeve, but record valuations meet softening guidance and REIT DPUs (Mapletree Industrial -4.9%) already reflect the rate drag. If the oil-led rate-hike narrative sticks, the REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT) are more exposed than the banks; watch the yield backdrop and the end-July MAS review.

items.headline: MAS reported to be imposing a single S-REIT leverage limit and added disclosures (pending confirmation)
items.summary: Singapore market coverage reports MAS is moving to a single aggregate-leverage limit and additional disclosure requirements for all SGX-listed REITs. The exact effective date and the numeric gearing cap were not confirmable from secondary sources this run and should be verified against the MAS primary release before acting. It would directly touch the portfolio's S-REIT sleeve.
items.actionable: A single leverage cap is a double-edged change for the S-REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT, CapLand China Trust) — clearer rules and more disclosure vs a potential constraint on gearing/acquisitions. Flagged as reported-but-unconfirmed: confirm the cap and date on the MAS site before repositioning the REIT sleeve.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips toward ~$64k, Ether ~$1,855, Solana ~$75 as oil-driven yields hit risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin traded in the mid-$60,000s (~$64k, after a ~$225M spot-ETF outflow), Ether around $1,855 (-2.5% 24h) and Solana ~$75 (-3.8% 24h) into the weekend as higher oil, tariff-driven inflation expectations and rising Treasury yields pulled money out of risk assets. Crypto is trading purely off the macro rate/yield channel; alternative.me Fear & Greed sits at ~27 (Fear). No distinct Sat/Sun tick verified — treat as Friday levels.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is moving in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade — the same Iran de-escalation catalyst that would help silver would relieve crypto. Treat it as a risk-appetite barometer; there is no crypto-specific bullish driver right now, and the EU's new offshore-crypto sanctions add a mild overhang.

items.headline: Tencent fires manager over leaked pay; Xiaomi's on-device MiMo LLM cleared; SMIC sees southbound selling
items.summary: Tencent fired a manager whose seven-figure compensation package leaked and went viral on Chinese social media (24 Jul). In flows, Tencent drew southbound net buying (~HK$2.3bn) while SMIC saw net selling (~HK$1.08bn); Xiaomi's self-developed on-device MiMo model passed China's national LLM registry filing — an AI-positive catalyst for the phone/EV maker.
items.actionable: Idiosyncratic single-stock noise inside the HK-tech core: Tencent's headline is cosmetic and its southbound buying is the better tell; Xiaomi's model approval is a genuine AI catalyst; SMIC's net selling is a mild near-term flow drag. Nets to holding Tencent as the core with Xiaomi as the higher-beta AI catch-up.

items.headline: Trump EO bars defense contractors from adversary-sourced critical materials — rare-earth reshoring tailwind
items.summary: Trump signed an executive order (20 Jul) further barring US defense contractors from sourcing critical materials from adversaries and directing the Pentagon to mitigate supply-chain national-security risks. It reinforces the structural US rare-earth reshoring push that already includes the DoD's ~15% MP Materials stake, a $110/kg NdPr price floor and a 10-year magnet offtake, plus ~$1.2bn of OSC loans (Energy Fuels, Phoenix Tailings) in June.
items.actionable: Another layer of Western government demand under the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — bullish MP and government-backed UUUU most directly. But with China's export controls suspended to 10 Nov (magnet exports +75% MoM), near-term pricing urgency is eased: accumulate on weakness into the control-snap-back catalyst rather than chase.

items.headline: EU adopts 21st Russia sanctions package — largest in 4 years, targets crypto rails
items.summary: The EU Council adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package — 218 listings, the largest batch in four years — targeting energy, banks, the shadow fleet and crypto. It bans transactions with 14 offshore crypto platforms and creates authority to blanket-ban crypto services from entire third countries facilitating sanctions evasion. Rubio and Lavrov met on the ASEAN sidelines in Manila on 23 July, keeping a diplomatic channel open.
items.actionable: A structural tightening of offshore crypto rails adds regulatory overhang to the crypto sleeve — a reason to keep crypto exposure modest versus the metals core; low direct relevance to the portfolio beyond that.
